title: Two clarinets in one band; Piku and Neely Barnes
summary: With two clarinets they made separate variations; Piku wrote him a second part to High Society.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: With that? With two clarinets and then one dance band? Yeah. Piku would double, but he'd use the saxophone. One guy would play high register, one guy low, or play the same thing, or what?

Well, we didn't play the same, you know, so we'd just go ahead and make all of them. Just make your own variations. Yeah. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know.
I don't know. You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same.

You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same. Like on high society, well, it'd be good. We'd make the same variation, but I'd make a second to it, you see. Piku had written out a second for me. And I don't know what happened to that clarinet. Because that was in Orlando, the band, too. So Piku was there, too? That was after something happened to his saxophone play. He got a regular job and he left the band. He took people in the band. Well, I heard you one night in Washington, in Germany, I think it was. Remember that joint up there? I think Howard wasn't able to make it one night, so he came up and you and Neely Bonds played together. And one would play up a register and another would play low. So they worked it out that way. If I'm not mistaken, you had your trombone. That's right. That's right.
I think I... How would you describe Dick Allen's trombone play? Terrible. Yeah, that's right. Did you ever hear Neely Bonds in the old days play? Yeah, I see.
